answer.rationale: With the line at 94% of committed volume and no buffer, switching the primary vendor within a 14-day window carries meaningful delivery-risk exposure that memory_c2 doesn't address (it speaks only to cost, onboarding speed, and invoicing accuracy, not to sustained delivery performance under full production load). Memory_c4 shows that renegotiating at renewal using competitive benchmarking (including the low-cost vendor's quote as leverage) can recover real margin and improve terms without the migration risk of a full vendor switch. Given the mandate can plausibly be met via negotiated concessions from the incumbent while preserving proven delivery stability (memory_c1), negotiate_terms is the safer single move this cycle. I'm verifying c2 and c4 because they directly weigh the cost-savings option against the renegotiation option, which is the core tradeoff here. I flag downstream risk because the low-cost vendor's true delivery reliability under full committed volume remains unverified, and defer full switch/second-sourcing decisions to the next review cycle rather than treating this negotiated outcome as proof of superiority.
